full_judgment:
2. The short fact leading to this Rule is that, opposite parties 1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Partition Suit No. 150 of 1964 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Comilla against the present petitioners and others and the same was decreed in preliminary form on 13-6-67 and thereafter final decree was passed on 10-11-87 which was subsequently set aside. On 6-1-1993 the learned Assistant Judge accepted the commissioner's report and the preliminary decree was made final which was subsequently sealed and signed on 21-11-1993 and then Title Execution Case No.1 of 1993 was initiated for getting possession in the land and that execution proceeding is still pending. Thereafter defendants 8Ka-8Cha and 121 and defendants 67, 37, 1 Cha, 2 and the plaintiffs filed a petition under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure alleging, that the newly appointed commissioner has not distributed the saham in accordance with the preliminary decree and he has also not given to the defendants and allotted more land than some of the parties are entitled to. The learned Assistant Judge then after hearing the parties by his order dated 22-2-93 set aside, the final decree. The  petitioner then being aggrieved by the impugned order moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Mr. Syed Mahmud Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that when the final decree was sealed and signed by the trial Court a petition filed under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable. He further submits that if the final decree is to be questioned the aggrieved party may move the appellate Court and the same cannot be set aside under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Assistant Judge failed to appreciate the provision of law and illegally passed the order dated 22-2-93. 

 4. Mr. Md. Latifur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 11(c), on the other hand, submits that the final decree must be in accordance with the terms of the preliminary decree and if the same is found to be not in terms and if there is illegality in distribution of the proceeding land this may be interfered with and the learned Assistant Judge has not committed any illegality in passing the impugned order. 

 5. Admittedly, the trial Court accepted the Commissioners report and final decree was drawn up and the same was sealed and signed by the trial Court on 21-1-1993. Thereafter a petition was filed by the aforesaid parties under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the decree on the ground that it has not been drawn up in accordance with the preliminary decree and some of the parties have not been given any land. 

 6. There is nothing before this Court at this stage to hold that any of the parties preferred any appeal against the preliminary decree and admittedly previously another Commissioner was appointed for distribution of the Saham which was subsequently cancelled and a new Commissioner was appointed who submitted his report and there was no objection from either side against that Commissioner report and, as such, the report was accepted and the final decree was drawn up which was duly sealed and signed by the trial Court. It appears that against that final decree neither party moved any higher court in appeal; though there may be an appeal against the final decree, on the ground that the decree was not drawn up in accordance with the terms of the preliminary decree and also on the ground of non-distribution of land in terms of the preliminary decree. When the suit has been finally disposed of, with the signing and sealing of the final decree there cannot be any petition filed under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that decree cannot be interfered with under this provision of the Code. When the aggrieved party has other remedy available, the inherent power of the Court under section 151 of the Code cannot be invoked. The learned Assistant Judge committed illegality in interfering with the final decree under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It further appears that the trial Court interfered with the decree of the ground that when the commissioner submitted his report, the matter was not brought to the notice or the parties in the litigation and, as such, they failed to file any objection. But it is well-settled that when parties are aware that the matter has been referred to a Commissioner they must be vigilant. It appears that in the present case the parties were not vigilant and they took no steps in filing any objection against the Commissioner's report and their indolent act cannot be ground to set aside the final decree drawn up after long and arduous litigations. In arriving at this decision reliance is placed in the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 51 (Abdur Rahman & ors. vs. Sultan @ Sultan and ors). 

 7. Having given my anxious consideration to the materials on record and hearing the learned Advocates of both the sides I hold that the learned Assistant Judge committed illegality in setting aside the decree by order dated 22-2-93 and it requires interference.
